caption: The drawing depicts a formal garden divided into four quadrants, enclosed within a rectangular boundary. The top of the image has a decorative border featuring sketched outlines of various fruits, flowers, and foliage. Within the boundaries, there are green sections representing lawns or grassy areas, and four main garden beds bordered by tan or light brown walkways. The upper left and lower right quadrants each have symmetrical parterre designs with geometric paths and sections of green hedges, central medallion shapes in blue, yellow, or green, and circular accents in green at the corners. The upper right quadrant contains a circular design with a central yellow flower motif and four symmetrical green sections, surrounded by orangish-red borders. The lower left quadrant is divided into rectangular beds with narrow stripes, alternating in green and blue-gray, with dots of yellow running down the central columns of some strips. Two white garden structures with red roofs and blue architectural accents are placed at the junctions of the boundary and central walkways: one is at the center right, and the other at the bottom right corner. A large tan and red-roofed building or wall occupies the upper right corner, extending toward the center. The bottom right quadrant is labeled “The Stuyvesant Garden from the Castello Plan” with the numbers "16" and "60" on either side of the text, suggesting the year 1660. The entire composition is rendered in a combination of green, brown, tan, yellow, blue, and red colors, with careful linear and geometric arrangement of the garden beds and structures.
title: Peter Stuyvesant Garden
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
